scope: Proposition 6.2 (Forward mass) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 42. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For any sufficiently small fixed η > 0, a prepared certificate at threshold a gives a surviving set of terminal injective paths whose expected terminal input mean, with stopped paths counted as zero, is at least (1 − η)a. The input is pulled back successively and masked by no bad flag at every active layer. Its support is progression-free. At least a fraction ηa of terminal paths have mean at least (1 − 2η)a, after harmless adjustment of the loss constants. The rank-stop probability at layer h need only have inverse logarithmic cost polynomial in the data at layers ≥ h. Discards immediately after that layer can be requested warm-small after charging the feasible-center proportions of layers > h. Thus this proposition does not require a lower-layer width in a higher-layer rank budget.
